chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from someone else, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
The looking at the private part of the one who is not a Muslim is like looking at the private part of the donkey.

key_terms.النَّظَرُ: The act of looking or gazing

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on looking at the private parts of a non-Muslim in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi’s chapter on the bathhouse, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a comparative legal ruling on modesty, equating the gaze at a non-Muslim’s awrah to that of a donkey. This analogy highlights the juristic distinction between human dignity and animal status in Islamic law, suggesting that while non-Muslims possess awrah, their concealment may not carry the same spiritual weight as that of a Muslim. It serves as a practical guideline for social interactions and privacy in mixed-religious contexts within Shia fiqh.
